### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**49** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c826e8a156ad3b839feaa4c7eefb63d63a4f3611`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (5 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c826e8a156ad3b839feaa4c7eefb63d63a4f3611` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c609159d8f87d05de1a85059a38ed7d78db44724` — the merge of head `39602028d251d5602bc4249f77b861d81cdb8e04` into base `c826e8a156ad3b839feaa4c7eefb63d63a4f3611`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c609159d8f87d05de1a85059a38ed7d78db44724 && git checkout c609159d8f87d05de1a85059a38ed7d78db44724
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c826e8a156ad3b839feaa4c7eefb63d63a4f3611 39602028d251d5602bc4249f77b861d81cdb8e04 && git checkout -B drift-repro c826e8a156ad3b839feaa4c7eefb63d63a4f3611 && git merge --no-ff 39602028d251d5602bc4249f77b861d81cdb8e04

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c826e8a156ad3b839feaa4c7eefb63d63a4f3611
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c826e8a156ad3b839feaa4c7eefb63d63a4f3611` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6039ced1af9e643038f44cdacb0d6fa32a6134d9`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #37766 (body and both comments: triage 7208015907, claim 7209168436), this PR's body, its 24 files and the net diff at the head, ADR-0162 (D5 and Execution item 7) on `main`, and the code the diff calls on `main` (`builtin/map-node.ts`, `builtin/subflow-node.ts`, `engine.ts#bubbleToParent`, `run-resume.ts#resumeInternal`, `runtime/src/domains/automation.ts#buildAutomationContext`). Check-runs on the head: every one that ran is `success` (Build Core, all Type Check, Test Core 1-10, Lint families, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI); the rest `skipped` by path. Those are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface and accept-set changes the diff implies:

- **`AutomationEngine.rootRunOf` / `recordRunOf`** (new members), **`RootRun` / `RecordRun`** (new type exports from `service-automation`'s index): right. Engine-local readers in the shape of `flowKeyOfRun`; additive.
- **Context keys `$rootRun` / `$recordRun`**: right. `$`-prefixed, so engine-owned (`engine.ts#isEngineVariable`); string keys survive the JSON round trip of a suspension. A top-level run overwrites whatever the caller handed (small call 6), and the HTTP door builds a whitelisted context (`buildAutomationContext`), so no caller reaches `$parentRunId` or either stamp from outside. `subflow` and `map` both build the child from the parent's context (`subflow-node.ts`, `map-node.ts`), so the inherited stamp is the parent's.
- **Stamp sites** (`execute()` and `dag-traversal.ts#executeWithoutRetry`): right. Those are the two run-context builders that run nodes; `dry-run.ts` also calls `resolveRunContext` but simulates the approval category and never runs the node executor. The only resume path that runs a segment is `resumeInternal`, so the derivation covers every legacy run that can reach an approval step.
- **Derivation** (`root-run.ts#deriveRunLinks`, called from `resumeInternal` before the claim, on a copy of the segment context): right. It goes through the strict loader, is bounded at 32 hops (that also ends a cycle), and its record-run rule matches `stampRootRun`'s (compare the child with its immediate parent while going up, versus compare with the inherited record run; the two agree because a record run's record is the record of every run under it). The `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` arm reuses the envelope and the not-consumed guarantee of the strict load of the run itself.
- **`ApprovalAutomationSurface.rootRunOf?` / `recordRunOf?`** and **`openNodeRequest` inputs `rootRun?` / `recordRun?`**: right, all optional. An older engine leaves the columns empty (pinned).
- **`sys_approval_request`**: `root_run_id`, `root_run_started_at`, `record_run_id` (nullable, readonly, engine-written at open), two indexes, two ids in `searchableFields` beside `flow_run_id`: right. They have the same shape as `flow_run_id` (text, maxLength 100). Schema sync adds them nullable, so there is nothing to migrate, as the changeset says. The translation bundles carry all three keys in all eleven locales.
- **The approval node's new refusal** (`approval-node.ts`: `rootRun === undefined || recordRun === undefined` fails the step): **wrong**, see M1.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37766-root-run.md`: `@objectstack/service-automation` patch, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, in the body and on the PR. No authorable key moves, so `none` is right, and under AGENTS.md post-task rule 3 `none` takes `patch` on both. The widening arm is right for every additive member listed in ①. It holds **only once M1 is resolved**: with the refusal kept, an approval step that opens on `main` (a legacy child whose parent is no longer parked) fails instead. That is a narrowing of what the node accepts, and the line would then owe `(narrowing)`, its BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 disposition. The card's "its own changeset and semver line" is met in substance: the one file names service-automation with its own level and its own bullet (N4).

### ③ Boundary flags

The six small calls:

1. **Two root-run columns (id and start; flow and object not stored).** Upheld. ADR-0162 D5 and Execution item 7 have slice C ask, at abandonment, whether a request that records no root run "was opened since the approval's run started". The run's context is gone by then, so the start has to be on the row. Slice B reads the flow and the object at open, where the node hands them.
2. **Record identity is `(object, record.id)`, with a numeric id read as its string.** Upheld. `map-node.ts` treats only a string-id item as a record. A numeric-id item therefore keeps the parent's `record` in its context and inherits the parent's record run. That is the outcome the definition intends.
3. **What a failed derivation does.** Split. The unreadable-parent arm (refuse the resume with `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`, nothing consumed, retryable) is upheld. So is stamping `null` with one `warn` and continuing. Refusing the approval step is **not** upheld: M1.
4. **Semver.** Upheld, conditional on M1 (see ②).
5. **The root's flow member is the slot key** (`SuspendedRun.flowName`). Upheld. It is the start key, which is "the flow it was started on" in the ADR's words, and the key slice B reads the flow back by.
6. **A stale caller `$rootRun` / `$recordRun` is overwritten; only `$parentRunId` makes a child.** Upheld. See ①: no external door can supply `$parentRunId`.

The card's six carried notes (N43, N44, N45, N17, N20, N21) belong to slices B and C. None is owed here.

SQL push-down: no finding. The diff's purpose is the push-down: slices B and C will filter the request table on indexed columns instead of reading `node_config_json` snapshots in the app. The one walk, `deriveRunLinks`, goes over the suspended-run store's keyed loader, which is not a SQL table. It runs once per run parked before the release and is bounded at 32 loads; the PR body states both.

**Must-fix**

- **M1. The approval node refuses a run whose root run could not be derived, which ADR-0162 does not do.** `approval-node.ts` fails every approval step whose run is stamped `null` (a run parked before the release whose parent is no longer parked, or a child of one). It does this whatever the object declares, and today the closed-states key is not published. ADR-0162 D5 and Execution item 7 handle exactly this population (requests opened before requests recorded their root run) in another way. Slice B leaves a request it "cannot place as first or later" **not judged**; slice C sends an abandoned request "that records no root run" **down the order**. The card adds "In an application with no declaration nothing is read", and the ADR adds "An approval that is read whole and reaches no step the conditions concern is refused nothing". "An approval it cannot read whole is refused" is the check's rule about the approval's flows, applied where the object closes on the field. It is not a rule about the run tree. On `main` such a child's approval opens, and `bubbleToParent` is best-effort when the child ends. Under this diff the run fails with an English-only message. Fix: open the request with null `root_run_id` / `root_run_started_at` / `record_run_id`, as the older-engine arm already does, and invert the "cannot be read whole" pin to show that the step opens and the columns are empty. Or take the refusal to the seat for a ruling that amends D5, and declare the narrowing in ②.

**Should-fix**

- **S1. The ruling that defines `record_run_id` is not on the card.** The PR body cites "the seat's ruling", and the column is recorded on every request. The card's two comments are triage and claim, and its body names only the root run. Slices B and C, and their reviewers, will key "an approval of its own" for a `map` item on this column. Put the ruling, or a pointer to it with its three pins (root run, record `map` item, `subflow` child that inherits), on #37766. This is seat-side and does not block the diff once M1 is fixed.

**Nits**

- **N1.** `approval-service.ts`: the two new interfaces are inserted between `ApprovalNodeAutoOutcome`'s JSDoc and its declaration. That block now sits on `ApprovalRootRun`, and the exported `ApprovalNodeAutoOutcome` has no doc. Move the insert above the block.
- **N2.** `request-root-run.integration.test.ts`: the comment "Hosts the two steps in a `subflow` child" is stranded above `BATCH`'s comment, and `PARENT` has none. Move it down to `PARENT`.
- **N3.** `RootRun.object` is documented as "the object of the root run's record; `null` on a record-less start", but `stampRootRun` and `deriveRunLinks` take `context.object` with or without a record. A manual launch carrying `objectName` and no `recordId` stamps an object. Either read it only beside a record id, or reword the doc.
- **N4.** The card's Done-when asks for the automation-service change to carry "its own changeset". It shares one file with the plugin. The judgement is made per package, so this has no effect on the release, and splitting the file is optional.
- **N5.** `ApprovalRootRun` / `ApprovalRecordRun` are part of `openNodeRequest`'s signature on the exported `ApprovalService`, but are not re-exported from the plugin's `index.ts`, where `ApprovalNodeAutoOutcome` is.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-3091w8`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `39602028d251d5602bc4249f77b861d81cdb8e04`
Local-runs: none

Delta round on the first record, 7210688247 (FAIL at `6039ced1`). Read for this round:

- the net diff `6039ced1...39602028` (one commit, no rebase; 8 files: the changeset, `approval-node.ts`, `approval-service.ts`, the plugin's `index.ts`, the integration test, `root-run.ts`, `run-resume.ts`, the ADR anchor);
- the seat ruling on #37766, 7210700837;
- the PR body as updated (Review rounds, small call 3, Tests);
- the check-runs on the new head: 39 `success` (Check Changeset, Build Core, every Type Check, Test Core 1-10, the Lint families, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI among them) and 18 `skipped` by path, none failed.

Nothing was re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

The first record's judgments stand on every surface the delta does not touch. The two it touches:

- **The approval node's refusal is removed.** It is now `rootRun = automation.rootRunOf?.(context) ?? null` and `recordRun = automation.recordRunOf?.(context) ?? null`, with no early return. A run the engine could not place now opens its step with the three columns null, the same row an engine without `rootRunOf` writes. Right. The optional call keeps `this` bound to the surface. A well-formed root with a malformed record run records the root and a null `record_run_id`, which is a request slice B and slice C already read as "records no record run".
- **`ApprovalRootRun` / `ApprovalRecordRun` are re-exported** from `plugin-approvals`' index beside `ApprovalNodeAutoOutcome`. Right: additive, type-only.

The engine side changes only prose: the `run-resume.ts` comment and the `warn` sentence, which now say that a request opened by such a run records none and no longer say that an approval step refuses. The `RootRun` and `RecordRun` docs and the ADR anchor invariant change in the same way. No behaviour moves there.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: both packages `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, in the PR body and in the changeset. With the refusal gone, nothing that opens on `main` is refused, so the widening arm is now true without condition, as the seat ruling 7210700837 states. The changeset's plugin bullet now says that an unplaced run opens its step as before with the columns empty, and that the two types are exported. That matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

Each finding of 7210688247, by id:

- **M1: closed.** The node no longer refuses, as the seat ruled on #37766 (7210700837): a run that cannot be placed opens with the three columns null, as the older-engine arm does. The pin is inverted. "a child whose tree cannot be read whole still opens its next step, with a request that records no root run" now asserts four things: `finalized` and `resumed` on the decision, the second request on `exec` in the same child run, all three columns null, and a child that has not failed. The PR body's small call 3 is rewritten to the ruling.
- **S1: closed.** The seat posted the `record_run_id` ruling and its three pins on #37766 (7210700837): the root run, a record `map` item, and a `subflow` child that inherits.
- **N1: closed.** `ApprovalNodeAutoOutcome`'s JSDoc sits on it again, below the two new interfaces.
- **N2: closed.** The stranded comment moved from above `BATCH` to `PARENT`.
- **N3: closed.** The docs now say what the stamp reads: the context's `object`, with or without a record id. That holds in `RootRun` and `RecordRun`, in `ApprovalRootRun` and `ApprovalRecordRun`, in the changeset and in the anchor. The code was already doing this, so only the docs moved.
- **N4: closed.** One changeset file is kept, by the seat's call. The judgement is still made per package.
- **N5: closed.** The two types are exported from the plugin's index.

The delta raises no new dev flag and no open question. SQL push-down: the delta adds no read and no walk, so there is no finding.

No finding is open.
